directive.quote: Every engine job of the old Worker's rust-engine backlog rows works on the new engine, one to one or better.

preserve: only a file whose set-aside name was forgotten for good is a candidate (noteGone from the set-aside forget step); a file with no name is never one by itself
a file stays while any holder names it by any of its identities: a live name, a name still set aside, a move off its store in progress
a chunk leaves only when no other file, finished or uploading, uses it
one release row per stored object addressed by origin and key; a row already there is queued again
a page of noted files turns each unheld file into release rows and forgets its file, span, chunk and alias records at once
claim marks a page claimed; a claim that never reported back is claimed again after claim_stale_minutes
released needs one exact origin and key and finishes only claimed rows; released rows stay as the record of storage given back

mayRecord: an unclaimed release of the same object is cancelled by an upload, a claimed one or one finished after the write began (less recorded_margin_seconds) refuses the bytes and the sender sends again
releaseGoneBytes (old src/namespace.mjs:1907-1934): claim, remove from the store, report released, a page at a time inside the call's time; a failed removal stays claimed
the numbers candidates_per_page 50, keys_per_page 100, recorded_margin_seconds 120, claim_stale_minutes 30
allowed_deltas: SQLite tables and the key-only queue rebuild become record store scopes @account-files/release/{noted,waiting,done}; waiting and done rows are two scopes so a claim walks only what still waits
claim walks waiting rows in id order (BLAKE3 of origin and key), not queued_at order: a scope has one order; every row is still reached

holders are read from the file record itself: `names` (live names) and a new `set_aside` list kept by the carry (Tree::listed_in), and a store that takes no new bytes while moves.rs empties it stands for the old namespace_moves holder

chunk sharing is recorded on the chunk record (`used_by` the first upload, `shared` once a second uses it) instead of a join over a span table; a migrated chunk with no `used_by` is never released here and is counted as kept_chunks
Recently Deleted's day-count sweep is not in the Rust set-aside; forget_set_aside is the explicit forget step that notes files
the shared origin room pool (releaseOriginRoomOnce) is dropped: central shared storage
the daily pass every_hours / continue_after_seconds is dropped: no always-on default; a caller asks queue_release and release_gone_bytes
byDay, summary totals and the release rules' screen DATA (_rules, item_facts, orders, forecast_days, choices) are dropped: the storage screen's feature; list_released pages what was given back
Objects gains delete (one DELETE; 200, 204 and 404 are done); a port without one refuses
banned_substitutions: a file noted because it has no name
an object removed while a holder names its file
a chunk removed that another file's span names
a release row written into central storage
a timer that releases bytes on its own
